Former Liberal minister Philip Ruddock has been appointed by the Australian cabinet to review whether Australian law properly protects the human right to religious freedom.

***

The appointment, announced on Wednesday, is intended in part to avoid a divisive fight over proposed religious amendments to same-sex marriage legislation. However, treasurer Scott Morrison said the review should not replace those amendments.

***

Prime minister Malcolm Turnbull said the issue of religious freedom needs careful examination following the yes vote on marriage equality and ahead of related legislation. He noted that a range of proposals had been raised in recent months, many extending beyond the immediate marriage debate.

***

There is disagreement within the government over timing. Some senior conservatives, including Peter Dutton and Mathias Cormann, have suggested a religious freedom bill could be dealt with next year as a separate matter, while Morrison and Liberal senator David Fawcett argue it should be addressed alongside the marriage bill.

***

Ruddock has been asked to report by 31 March. Turnbull said any broader reforms must be handled cautiously because poorly framed protections for rights such as freedom of religion could create unintended consequences, and he described Ruddock as well qualified for the task because of his experience as Australia’s special envoy for human rights.
